quests.hint: Verb meaning to cook food for too little time. If you ____ the chicken, it can be unsafe to eat.
quests.explanation: UNDER- + COOK = UNDERCOOK. The prefix UNDER- means 'too little', the opposite of the OVER- you saw with OVERCOOK - together they show how one root can grow in two directions.

quests.hint: Verb meaning to guess a number or amount as lower than it really is. The team badly ____ how long the repairs would take.
quests.explanation: UNDER- + ESTIMATE = UNDERESTIMATE. Adding UNDER- to ESTIMATE creates a verb meaning to judge something as smaller or less than it actually is.

quests.hint: Verb meaning to give someone less money than their work deserves. Workers protested after learning the factory would ____ new staff.
quests.explanation: UNDER- + PAY = UNDERPAY. The prefix UNDER- shows insufficiency, so UNDERPAY means to pay less than what is fair or expected.

quests.hint: Verb meaning to watch or look at something before it's officially released. Fans lined up to ____ the trailer for the new film.
quests.explanation: PRE- + VIEW = PREVIEW. The prefix PRE- means 'before', so PREVIEW means to view something ahead of its release.

quests.hint: Verb meaning to warm an oven before putting food inside. Don't forget to ____ the oven to 350 degrees.
quests.explanation: PRE- + HEAT = PREHEAT. Adding PRE- to HEAT creates a verb meaning to heat something in advance.

quests.hint: Verb meaning to pay for something before you receive it. Many hotels ask guests to ____ for the first night's stay.
quests.explanation: PRE- + PAY = PREPAY. This continues the PAY family from an earlier level: PAY, UNDERPAY, and now PREPAY, meaning to pay ahead of time.

quests.hint: Adjective describing someone who avoids spending time with other people. He's fairly ____ and prefers reading alone to going to parties.
quests.explanation: ANTI- + SOCIAL = ANTISOCIAL. The prefix ANTI- means 'against', so ANTISOCIAL describes behavior that goes against normal social contact.

quests.hint: Noun for software that protects a computer from harmful programs. Every laptop in the office needs updated ____ installed.
quests.explanation: ANTI- + VIRUS = ANTIVIRUS. Adding ANTI- to VIRUS names something designed to work against viruses.

quests.hint: Noun for a liquid added to a car's engine to stop it from freezing. Check your ____ level before the winter road trip.
quests.explanation: ANTI- + FREEZE = ANTIFREEZE. The prefix ANTI- shows opposition, so ANTIFREEZE is a substance that works against freezing.

quests.hint: Noun for a fast underground train system in a city. We took the ____ to get across downtown during rush hour.
quests.explanation: SUB- + WAY = SUBWAY. The prefix SUB- means 'under' or 'below', so SUBWAY literally describes a road or path running underground.

quests.hint: Noun for the translated text shown at the bottom of a movie screen. I turned on the ____ because the actors spoke so quietly.
quests.explanation: SUB- + TITLE = SUBTITLE. Adding SUB- to TITLE names text placed below the main picture, showing translated or extra dialogue.

quests.hint: Noun for a smaller group formed within a larger committee. The board created a ____ to focus only on the new budget.
quests.explanation: SUB- + COMMITTEE = SUBCOMMITTEE. The prefix SUB- shows a smaller unit existing beneath a larger one, here inside a committee.

quests.hint: Adjective describing something involving more than one country. The company signed a major ____ trade deal last spring.
quests.explanation: INTER- + NATIONAL = INTERNATIONAL. The prefix INTER- means 'between', so INTERNATIONAL describes something happening between nations - this reuses the NATIONAL you met earlier.

quests.hint: Verb meaning to talk or work together with someone. Students were asked to ____ with a partner during the science project.
quests.explanation: INTER- + ACT = INTERACT. Adding INTER- to ACT means to act in a way that involves another person - a new branch of the ACT family from earlier levels.

quests.hint: Noun for a formal conversation used to evaluate a job candidate. She stayed calm through every question in the ____.
quests.explanation: INTER- + VIEW = INTERVIEW. The prefix INTER- means 'between', so INTERVIEW describes a structured exchange of views between two people - continuing the VIEW family from PREVIEW.

quests.hint: Verb meaning to work together toward a shared goal. The two departments agreed to ____ on the new product launch.
quests.explanation: CO- + OPERATE = COOPERATE. The prefix CO- means 'together', so COOPERATE means to work jointly with someone else.

quests.hint: Noun for a person you work with at the same company. My ____ helped me finish the report before the deadline.
quests.explanation: CO- + WORKER = COWORKER. Adding CO- to WORKER names someone who works together with you.

quests.hint: Noun for the second person who helps fly a plane. The ____ took control while the captain rested.
quests.explanation: CO- + PILOT = COPILOT. The prefix CO- shows a shared role, so COPILOT names the pilot who shares flying duties with the captain.

quests.hint: Verb meaning to sell and send goods to another country. This factory started to ____ furniture to Europe last year.
quests.explanation: EX- + PORT = EXPORT. The prefix EX- means 'out', so EXPORT means to carry goods out of a country to sell elsewhere.

quests.hint: Verb meaning to pull or take something out, often with effort. Dentists sometimes need to ____ a badly damaged tooth.
quests.explanation: EX- + TRACT = EXTRACT. Adding EX- to TRACT (meaning 'to pull') forms a verb meaning to pull something out.

quests.hint: Verb meaning to breathe air out of your lungs. The yoga instructor told us to ____ slowly through the mouth.
quests.explanation: EX- + HALE = EXHALE. The prefix EX- means 'out', so EXHALE means to breathe air out, the opposite of INHALE.

quests.hint: Noun for the fact or state of being real or being present. Scientists debate whether there's proof of the ____ of life on other planets.
quests.explanation: EXIST + -ENCE = EXISTENCE. Adding -ENCE to the verb EXIST creates a noun naming the state of existing.

quests.hint: Noun for how well someone does a task or job. The coach reviewed each player's ____ after the match.
quests.explanation: PERFORM + -ANCE = PERFORMANCE. The suffix -ANCE turns the verb PERFORM into a noun naming the quality or result of an action.

quests.hint: Noun for help given to someone who needs it. The charity offers financial ____ to families affected by the flood.
quests.explanation: ASSIST + -ANCE = ASSISTANCE. This continues the ASSIST family from ASSISTANT in an earlier level, this time forming a noun for the help itself rather than the person who gives it.

quests.hint: Adjective describing something that fills you with amazement. The view from the mountain top was absolutely ____.
quests.explanation: WONDER + -FUL = WONDERFUL. Adding -FUL to the noun WONDER forms an adjective meaning 'full of wonder', or amazing.

quests.hint: Adjective describing a feeling of great happiness. The crowd was ____ when the home team scored the winning goal.
quests.explanation: JOY + -OUS = JOYOUS. The suffix -OUS turns the noun JOY into an adjective describing great happiness, similar in feel to -FUL but a different spelling pattern.

quests.hint: Adjective describing smooth, elegant movement. The ice skater made the difficult jump look ____.
quests.explanation: GRACE + -FUL = GRACEFUL. Unlike suffixes that start with a vowel, -FUL starts with a consonant, so GRACE keeps its silent E: GRACE + FUL = GRACEFUL, not 'gracful'.

quests.hint: Noun for the smaller amount shown before tax is added. The receipt listed a ____ of forty dollars before tax.
quests.explanation: SUB- + TOTAL = SUBTOTAL. This reviews the SUB- pattern from SUBWAY and SUBTITLE earlier, this time attached to the noun TOTAL.

quests.hint: Noun for someone who sings, acts, or plays music for an audience. The ____ took a bow as the audience clapped loudly.
quests.explanation: PERFORM + -ER = PERFORMER. This root already gave you PERFORMANCE in an earlier level; adding -ER instead names the person who performs rather than the act itself.

quests.hint: Verb meaning to trade one thing for another. Customers can ____ a damaged item for a new one within thirty days.
quests.explanation: EX- + CHANGE = EXCHANGE. This reviews the EX- pattern from EXPORT and EXTRACT earlier, this time attached to the verb CHANGE to mean trading one thing for another.
